scores.reason: Biochemical proof of endogenous hyperinsulinism at documented hypoglycaemia is the defining step before localisation and surgery, and no other test substitutes (rule 15). Thresholds reach the project second-hand through ENETS, and the Endocrine Society text was read at abstract level only, so 3 is the alternative.

anchor_issues: Row 1 D1: whether the 4 anchor (guideline requires the result before the decision) is met when the requirement is the diagnostic definition, not a stated 'must test before surgery' sentence. Chose 4 with medium confidence; 3 is the alternative.
Row 29 D1: the label requirement is regulatory, but ADA 2026 predates and does not endorse the Stage 3 indication, so which status is current is unclear. Chose 4 (label), confidence medium.
Row 23 and 22 D6: anchor 3 'low (reversible, minor)' and 1 'notable' do not say how to score a supervised provocative test; chose by the lower of burden and consequence.

Stakes rows 1, 2, 24, 23: the anchor boundary between 3 (serious morbidity) and 4 (life-threatening or irreversible) is not tied to the typical outcome; chose 3 where permanent harm is possible but not typical.
assumptions: No new searches were run; every score rests on usecases-verified.md rows and the rubric. Guideline thresholds and read levels are as the project recorded them, and I did not re-open PubMed or the label. DOIs were not re-checked here because the rows in the project file list PMIDs only.
Setting tags: row 1 is tagged specialist outpatient although a 72-hour fast is usually an admission; the first-contact sample is often taken in the emergency department.
Row 29 assumes the project's skeptic-verified label text (rev 06/2026) is current.
